newsitem.title: UK: CE renews attack on Northern after results.
newsitem.headline: CE renews attack on Northern after results.

text.p: CE Electric, the British bid vehicle of U.S. energy group CalEnergy, said on Friday interim results from its hostile bid target Northern Electric Plc were below it expectations and confirmed its belief that its 630p cash per share offer represented full value.
"CE Electric is disappointed by Northern Electric's lacklustre profit performance which fell below its expectations," the company said in a statement.
Northern Electric reported half-year pre-tax profits of 50.7 million pounds and paid out a dividend of 12.85 pence, while its interim gearing stood at 47 percent.

Northern said gearing without the special dividend, which would lapse if CE Electric won control, would be roughly in line with other regional electricity companies and argued that based on 1997 forecast cashflow, it should be valued at 745 pence.
CE Electric said Northern had reduced pension charges and claimed it had "reassessed" proceeds due from asset disposals.

CE Electric's chairman and chief executive David Sokol said: "Following the publication of these results, it has become even clearer that without CE Electric's offer, Norhern Electric's ordinary sahres would be worth much less than 630 p".
"Our ordinary offer remains the only way for shareholders to receive 630p in cash for their ordinary shares," said Sokol.
Norrthern's share price had fallen to 585 from Thursday's close of 590 but edged ahead to 593 towards close of trade at 1600 GMT.
